title: CS KPI Lexicon and Operational Workbook - latency / uptime / cost-per-token / cache-hit
content:
Purpose:
To standardize how we compute, display, and action four core QBR signals used in renewal and operational conversations: latency, uptime/availability, cost-per-token, and cache-hit rate. This is a working reference + compact workbook intended for Customer Success directors and Solutions Engineers preparing QBR slides and renewal risk analysis.

Audience:
CS managers, Solutions Eng, Observability/Platform SMEs, and Product managers preparing customer-ready KPI snapshots.

Quick note on scope and style:
- This is intentionally concise and operational (how to measure, sample queries, typical thresholds, and a simple QBR table).
- Keep this doc lightweight; migrate final formats into the QBR template deck after signoff.

1) Latency (primary user-facing measure)
Definition: end-to-end request latency measured from Redwood ingress (received HTTP request) to first-token emitted to the client, plus time-to-last-token when we report generation completion.
Why it matters: Directly affects user experience and perceived product performance. High p95/p99 spikes are more impactful in conversations than small changes to p50.
Common variants we use:
  - p50 / p95 / p99 (end-to-end) per route or API key
  - server-gen-per-token (ms/token) measured on serving nodes for load characterization
Measurement window: 5m rolling for alerts, 7d and 28d aggregates for QBR snapshots.
PromQL examples (approx):
  - p95 end-to-end /route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
  - server-side gen ms/token: 1000 * sum(rate(model_generation_time_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(model_generation_tokens_total[5m]))
Suggested SLOs (example):
  - Startup (low-latency offering): p95 < 600 ms, p99 < 1.5s
  - Mid-market: p95 < 800 ms, p99 < 2.5s
  - Enterprise (large-batch workloads): p95 < 1s (but measure separate batch/stream paths)
Alerting guidance:
  - Fire page when p99 exceeds target for 15m and error rate concurrently > 0.5%
  - Inform CS when p95 increases > 30% vs 28d baseline and sustained for > 24h
Known gotchas:
  - Client-side network jitter vs server processing: prefer server-side timing for root cause (use tracing).
  - Cold-starts: isolate warm vs cold-start latency in dashboards to avoid misleading spikes.

2) Uptime / Availability
Definition: percentage of successful production requests over total scheduled checks (or successful health-checks) for the configured service surface (hosted API endpoints + control plane as appropriate). For customer-facing SLO, use 99.9/99.95 windows depending on plan.
Formula: uptime = 1 - (total_downtime_seconds / total_period_seconds)
Data sources: synthetic uptime checks (external), internal ingress 5xx rate, and SRE incident logs.
Measurement windows: 30d rolling for QBR; 90d for contractual review.
Example SQL (pseudo):
  SELECT (1 - SUM(downtime_seconds)/SUM(period_seconds)) as uptime FROM uptime_checks WHERE service_id = 'api' AND ts BETWEEN X AND Y;
SLA vs SLO: use SLA only when tied to contract; otherwise present SLO and error budget consumption.
Action thresholds for CS:
  - Report to customer when monthly uptime < agreed SLO (or if error budget > 25% used).
  - For incidents > 30 minutes impacting the customer, attach incident summary to QBR materials.

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
Definition: normalized platform cost divided by output tokens (or billable tokens, depending on customer billing setup). Be explicit whether you include infra, data transfer, and model-licensing costs.
Primary formulas (pick one consistently):
  - cost_per_output_token = (platform_cost_allocated_to_customer_period) / (output_tokens_generated)
  - cost_per_billable_token = total_invoice_cost / billable_token_units
Measurement notes:
  - For fairness, separate input tokens from output tokens in heavy prompt workloads. Report both if customer prompts are large (they materially change unit economics).
  - Show both raw cost and adjusted cost (after caching/response-reuse).
Typical threshold bands (illustrative):
  - High-volume startup: $0.0006 - $0.002 per output token (depends on model family & quantization)
  - Mid-market: $0.0009 - $0.003
  - Enterprise: negotiate committed pricing / reserved capacity (use Redwood Dedicated assumptions)
QBR tip: present a 3-row table: baseline (last quarter avg), optimized (with cache & batching), and projected (after guidance).

4) Cache-hit rate (user-level prefix/KV cache)
Definition: proportion of requests served partially or wholly from cache (prefix/KV) rather than cold model execution.
Formula: cache_hit_rate = hits / (hits + misses) over the measurement window. For prefix caches, define hit when prefix match length >= N tokens (document how N is chosen).
PromQL snippet (conceptual):
  sum(rate(prefix_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(prefix_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(prefix_cache_misses_total[5m]))
Why it matters: cache hits directly reduce latency and cost-per-token and are a critical levers for performance-oriented customers.
Common pitfalls:
  - Tokenization mismatch between client and server can under-report hits. 
  - Privacy settings: some customers disable prefix caching entirely; document this in the QBR.
Suggested targets for discussion:
  - Good: > 15% overall (for interactive apps with reused prompts)
  - Excellent: > 35% (high reuse patterns, templated prompts)

5) Compact QBR KPI Table (copy into slide)
Columns: Metric | Definition (one-liner) | Source (query or check) | Target | Last quarter | Owner | Actionable note
Example row block (paste-ready):
Metric | Definition | Source | Target | Last quarter | Owner | Actionable note
Latency p95 | 95th pct end-to-end latency (ms) | prom: histogram_quantile(0.95,...route...) | < 800 ms | 940 ms | Platform SRE | Investigate recent rollout; enable warm caches
Uptime (30d) | % of successful requests | external uptime checks / incidents | >= 99.95% | 99.92% | SRE | Provide incident RCA and mitigation timeline
Cost / output token | Platform cost divided by output tokens | billing/finance export + redwood-cost-allocation | <$0.0012 | $0.0018 | Customer Success / Finance | Review batching and model family choices; propose caching pilot
Cache hit rate | prefix + KV hit proportion | prom: prefix_cache_hits / (hits+misses) | > 20% | 8% | Solutions Eng | Identify top prompt patterns for caching; ask devs to template reuse

6) Operational playbook snippets (what to do during prep)
  - Pull 28d rolling metrics and 7d trend for the KPIs (both absolute and pct change).
  - For latency/cost issues, correlate with model rollout tags and infra events (use traces).
  - If cache-hit < target: run a short review with solutions eng to map top 10 prompt families and propose caching rules.
  - For uptime blips: attach incident timeline and show error budget consumption in slide.

7) Sample QBR slide checklist (short)
  - One-line health summary (Green/Yellow/Red) with the primary reason
  - KPI table (from section 5) with trends + action owner
  - Two operational recommendations with expected delta (cost or latency)
  - Open risks (incidents, usage growth > 3x, prompt changes)
  - Next steps and owners (who will run pilot, timeline)

8) Notes-to-self / TODOs
  - [ ] Validate PromQL snippets with Observability (SRE) and convert to exact metric names (today they are conceptual).
  - [ ] Generate an automated query that builds the QBR table snapshot (CSV export). Ticket: CS-421-collection
  - [ ] Synthesize a one-page handout that maps caching improvements to expected cost delta for common customer patterns.

9) References & related artifacts
  - Confluence: KPI Reference (linked above)
  - Jira: CS-378 (QBR automation), CS-421-collection (cache pilot requests)

If you use this doc to build the slide deck, please retain the query text under "Source" so Observability can reproduce numbers during QBR review. Mark finalized definitions with date and owner when we lock them into the template.

End of working draft.
